/-!
# Erdős Problem 303

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/303](https://www.erdosproblems.com/303)
- [BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit
  fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
-/

namespace Erdos303

/--
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

This is true, as proved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

This was formalized in Lean by Yuan using Seed-Prover.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/303"]
theorem erdos_303 :
    answer(True) ↔
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- There exists integers `a, b, c`
      ∃ (a b c : ℤ),
      -- that are non-zero and distinct.
      [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧
      -- `a, b, c` satisfy the equation
      (1/a : ℝ) = 1/b + 1/c ∧
      -- `a, b, c` have the same color
      (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton := by
  sorry

end Erdos303

reformulations.difference: Brown–Rödl's primary-paper formulation uses positive integers and arbitrary finite palettes. Lean instead uses finite-range integer-valued colourings of ℤ and permits nonzero signed witnesses. The problem webpage itself also says “integers.”
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The positive-integer statement implies the signed statement by restricting a colouring to positive inputs. Conversely, extend a positive colouring to nonzero integers by pairing the colour of |z| with the sign of z, and encode this finite palette in ℤ. A monochromatic signed solution then has one common sign. Taking absolute values preserves distinctness and the reciprocal equation, yielding a positive monochromatic solution. Zero is excluded by [a,b,c,0].Nodup. Finite-range integer labels and arbitrary finite palettes are interchangeable by relabelling. Both reductions were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; Review303.full_equivalence has no sorryAx dependency.
